surprises: OBSERVATION / INERT -- MY OWN DH-3 CHECK FAILED THE CRITERION FOR THE WRONG REASON, and the direction it failed in was the lucky one. A line-based filter over a00_runner.py reported three date 'literals in code'; all three were prose -- a --date usage example in the module docstring, an author line, and a trailing comment on a code line. A line filter cannot separate code from prose. Replaced with an AST walk over string constants excluding docstrings (comments never enter the tree) plus a targeted walk of attestation_epoch()'s own body; both empty. The transferable half: this instrument could just as easily have erred the other way and reported PASS over a genuinely typed epoch, and nothing downstream would have caught it -- the criterion's whole point is that a pinned date is invisible once it exists.

OBSERVATION / INERT -- A LOAD-BEARING COMMIT WAS BLOCKED BY ANOTHER SEAT'S LIVE git index.lock, AND THE CORRECT ACT WAS TO NOT RESOLVE IT. Two safe-commit attempts returned rc=128 on .git/index.lock while three seats were waiting on the line that commit carried. My instruments could establish only that the lock was QUIET -- unchanged size and mtime across a probe -- which is consistent with abandoned but is not proof of it, and MSYS ps structurally cannot see detached native git processes so 'no live git' was never evidence. I refused to delete it and reported the block instead. 1.0.0_SA_CTO then identified the holder with Windows-native enumeration as a LIVE git process waiting on a commit-message editor with a dead parent -- a write that could never finish, and one that deleting the lock would have raced. The lock later cleared by some means I did not observe and did not cause; the commit landed on retry. Recorded because the tempting act (delete a quiet lock on a shared tree) and the correct act (report and wait) look identical in cost right up until they don't.

OBSERVATION / INERT -- I REPORTED A BLOCKED ACT BEFORE RESOLVING IT, WHICH TURNED OUT TO MATTER. Because the block was surfaced immediately rather than after a fix, 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~L kept a correct hold on their unlock read instead of acting on an expectation, and no seat spent time on a line they believed was already in place. The inverse -- reporting the append as done and then discovering the commit had not landed -- was available and would have propagated a false state to three seats and a gated 531-partition pass.

OBSERVATION / INERT -- MY OWN ACCEPTANCE HARNESS LEFT AN UNTRACKED FILE IN THE PRODUCER TREE. DH-6's baseline module had to be written INTO data/assets/scripts/gold/runners_49f for its HERE.parents[4] path arithmetic to match the live module's -- a scratch-directory copy aborts at bootstrap. My first run left that temp file behind, untracked, in the tree that feeds the deploy. An untracked-but-present file is invisible to every count, listing, battery and predicate that would otherwise notice it, and the next safe-deploy sweep is exactly the sort of thing that could have picked it up. Removed, and cleanup is now IN the harness and IN its verdict -- the run FAILS if the temp survives, rather than relying on me to remember.
